326	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
327	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
328	template <OptId Opt>
329	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
330	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
331	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
332	    (void)step;  // referenced only by the cold-start branches (grokfast/grokadamw)
333	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
334	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
335	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
336	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
337	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
338	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
339	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
340	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
341	        // COLD-START (state-aware tail; owner baseline blocker (a)): the eager
342	        // Grokfast seeds the slow-grad EMA with the FIRST gradient, not zeros
343	        // (grokfast.py _group_cache: state["ema"] = grad0.clone()), because a
344	        // zero seed under-amplifies the early grokking phase and the kernel
345	        // applies no EMA bias correction. The persistent [m|v|extra] state cache
346	        // zero-inits ema=0, so at step 1 we must seed ema=grad HERE — then
347	        // grokfast_fused_step's e_new = alpha*g + (1-alpha)*g = g matches the
348	        // eager ema=grad0 exactly. Per-element on this thread's own idx (the P3
349	        // tail owns each element once), so no race / no barrier needed. For
350	        // step>1 the cache carries the real EMA forward (no reseed).
351	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];
352	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
353	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
354	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
355	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
356	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
357	        // FAITHFUL GrokAdamW (decoder L3-TC conversion) — all THREE eager
358	        // mechanisms now land, so the cell is no longer a hollow pass:
359	        //
360	        //  (i)  PER-TENSOR LAYER-WISE β1 = β1·(1-γ)^layer (grokadamw.py
361	        //       _layer_beta1_by_id). The caller (the P3 work-steal loop, which
362	        //       owns the tensor index t == the flat named_parameters() layer
363	        //       index) has ALREADY rebased st.beta1 to β1_i AND st.bc1 to
364	        //       1-β1_i^step for THIS tensor before calling us (see the
365	        //       fused_decoder_megakernel P3 block, guarded by if constexpr
366	        //       GrokAdamW). So st.beta1/st.bc1 here are the per-tensor values;
367	        //       this branch just consumes them. bc2 stays global (β2 is not
368	        //       layer-wise). This is the mechanism that fails the STATE gate at
369	        //       step 1 if dropped (m-rel 0.895), so it is load-bearing.
370	        //
371	        //  (ii) GLOBAL GRAD-NORM CLIP to grad_clip (bindings.cpp
372	        //       clip_grad_norms_device_side → a GLOBAL norm over ALL tensors,
373	        //       one scalar clip_coef = grad_clip/(‖g‖₂+1e-6) applied to every
374	        //       grad when ‖g‖₂ > grad_clip). The kernel computes ‖g‖₂ + clip_coef
375	        //       ON-DEVICE in P2.5 (deterministic ascending-CTA reduction over the
376	        //       reduced grad) and stashes st.clip_coef; we scale the grad by it
377	        //       HERE. Eager clips IN-PLACE before the ema-seed AND the step, so we
378	        //       use the SAME clipped grad for both. At step 1 ‖g‖₂≈0.72<1 ⇒
379	        //       clip_coef=1 (inert), but it FIRES multi-step — the missing-clip
380	        //       2e-4 divergence is what the multi-step parity check catches.
381	        //
382	        //  (iii) ADAPTIVE α = alpha_init·exp(-κ·signal): in-context this is a
383	        //       genuine NO-OP. No race/gate path feeds (train_loss, val_loss) to
384	        //       GrokAdamW.step(), so eager α stays at alpha_init for ALL steps =
385	        //       the static st.alpha bound here. Faithful, not dropped (verified:
386	        //       fused_train_step/fused_optimizer_step/race never pass losses).
387	        //
388	        // COLD-START: eager seeds ema = the UNCLIPPED grad0, NOT the clipped grad.
389	        // grokadamw.py _group_cache clones state["ema"] = p.grad.clone() (the raw
390	        // gradient) BEFORE grokadamw_fused_step's in-place clip_grad_norms_device_
391	        // side (bindings.cpp:215) runs — so the cold-start seed is the UNCLIPPED
392	        // grad while the EMA filter input + amplification use the CLIPPED grad. The
393	        // prior `st.ema[idx]=gc` seeded the CLIPPED grad, which is byte-identical
394	        // when the clip is INERT (clip_coef==1 ⇒ gc==grad) — every currently-green
395	        // config — but diverges the m/ema state when the clip FIRES (the forced-fire
396	        // multi-step parity surfaced this: kernel ema/clipped==1.0 vs eager 1/coef).
397	        // Fix: seed the UNCLIPPED grad; keep the filter + g_amp on gc.
398	        const float gc = grad[idx] * st.clip_coef;   // (ii) global-clipped grad
399	        if (step == 1) st.ema[idx] = grad[idx];       // cold-start on UNCLIPPED grad
400	        // EMA filter + amplification (csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h math), on gc.
401	        const float ema_new = st.alpha * st.ema[idx] + (1.0f - st.alpha) * gc;
402	        st.ema[idx] = ema_new;
403	        const float g_amp = gc + st.lamb * ema_new;
404	        // Adam moments + decoupled-WD apply: the canonical grokadamw_adam_tail
405	        // (bit-identical to grokadamw_step's tail), driven by the per-tensor
406	        // st.beta1/st.bc1 (i) and the un-inverted global st.bc2.
407	        float m_out, v_out, p_out;
408	        algo::grokadamw_adam_tail(
409	            g_amp, params[idx], st.exp_avg[idx], st.exp_avg_sq[idx],
410	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2,
411	            m_out, v_out, p_out);
412	        st.exp_avg[idx]    = m_out;
413	        st.exp_avg_sq[idx] = v_out;
414	        params[idx]        = p_out;
415	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
416	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
417	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
418	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
419	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
420	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
421	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
422	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
423	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
424	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
425	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
426	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
427	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
428	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
429	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
430	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
431	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
432	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
433	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
434	            fabsf(grad[idx]), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
435	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
436	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
437	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
438	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
439	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
440	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
441	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
442	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
443	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
444	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
445	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
446	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
447	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
448	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
449	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
450	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
451	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
452	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
453	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
454	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
455	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
456	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
457	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
458	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
459	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
460	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
461	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
462	    }
463	}

62	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
63	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
64	// =========================================================================
65	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
66	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
67	    unsigned id;
68	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
69	    return id;
70	#else
71	    return 0u;
72	#endif
73	}

75	// =========================================================================
76	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
77	//
78	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
79	//  Every CTA runs:
80	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
81	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
82	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
83	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
84	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
85	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
86	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
87	//
88	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
89	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
90	// =========================================================================
91	struct TaskQueue {
92	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
93	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
94	
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
96	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
97	
98	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
99	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
100	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
101	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
102	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
103	    }
104	
105	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
106	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
107	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
108	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
109	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
110	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
111	        }
112	        __syncthreads();
113	        int t = *smem_slot;
114	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
115	        return t;
116	    }
117	};
118	
119	// =========================================================================
120	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
121	//
122	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
123	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
124	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
125	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
126	//
127	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
128	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
129	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
130	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
131	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
132	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
133	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
134	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
135	//
136	//  Fences (§1.14):
137	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
138	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
139	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
140	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
141	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
142	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
143	//
144	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
145	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
146	// =========================================================================
147	struct GridBarrier {
148	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
149	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
150	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
151	
152	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
153	                                            unsigned* generation,
154	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
155	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
156	
157	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
158	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
159	        __syncthreads();
160	
161	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
162	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
163	            unsigned my_gen =
164	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
165	
166	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
167	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
168	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
169	            __threadfence();
170	
171	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
172	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
173	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
174	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
175	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
176	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
177	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
178	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
179	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
180	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
181	                __threadfence();
182	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
183	            } else {
184	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
185	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
186	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
187	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
188	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
189	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
190	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
191	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
192	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
193	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
194	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
195	                       == my_gen) {
196	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
197	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
198	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
199	#endif
200	                }
201	            }
202	
203	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
204	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
205	            __threadfence();
206	        }
207	
208	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
209	        __syncthreads();
210	    }
211	
212	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
213	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
214	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
215	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
216	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
217	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
218	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
219	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
220	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
221	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
222	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
223	        __syncthreads();
224	
225	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
226	            unsigned my_gen =
227	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
228	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
229	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
230	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
231	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
232	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
233	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
234	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
235	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
236	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
237	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
238	                __threadfence();
239	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
240	            } else {
241	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
242	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
243	                       == my_gen) {
244	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
245	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
246	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
247	#endif
248	                }
249	            }
250	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
251	        }
252	
253	        __syncthreads();
254	    }
255	};
256	
257	// =========================================================================
258	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
259	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
260	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
261	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
262	// =========================================================================
263	struct PersistentContext {
264	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
265	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
266	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
267	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
268	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
269	
270	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
271	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
272	    }
273	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
274	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
275	    }
276	};

222	//   Phase B: every CTA owner-sums the slots in fixed order and writes d to
223	//            ws.prodigy_d (== st.d_factor for the apply tail).
224	// ============================================================================
225	
226	// Phase A — accumulate this CTA's (r,s) partial over all its queued tensors and
227	// publish to the per-CTA slots. `param_init` is the Prodigy trajectory anchor
228	// (one flat blob parallel to params). Drains the SAME task queue the apply uses.
229	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseA(
230	        const PersistentContext& ctx,
231	        const float* __restrict__ params,
232	        const float* __restrict__ param_init,
233	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
234	        const int* __restrict__ sizes, const int* __restrict__ offsets,
235	        float d_prev,
236	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
237	    __shared__ int task_slot;
238	    float r_acc = 0.0f, s_acc = 0.0f;
239	    TaskQueue q = ctx.queue();
240	    for (int t = q.next_block(&task_slot); t < ctx.n_tasks;
241	         t = q.next_block(&task_slot)) {
242	        const int n = sizes[t];
243	        const int64_t off = (int64_t)offsets[t];
244	        for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
245	            // Canonical per-element partials (prodigy.h:28-53). r/s carry d² so
246	            // d_hat=r/s is scale-free; s is the L1 norm Σ d²·|g|.
247	            float r_one = 0.0f, s_one = 0.0f;
248	            algo::prodigy_partials_step(params + off, param_init + off, grad + off,
249	                                        d_prev, (int64_t)i, r_one, s_one);
250	            r_acc += r_one;
251	            s_acc += s_one;
252	        }
253	    }
254	    // Deterministic in-CTA reduction of this CTA's (r,s) — fixed thread count.
255	    float r_block, s_block;
256	    prim::block_reduce_sum2_f32(r_acc, s_acc, r_block, s_block);
257	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
258	        // Per-CTA slot publish (no atomic). r slots [0..n_ctas), s slots after.
259	        ws.prodigy_partials[blockIdx.x]              = r_block;
260	        ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + blockIdx.x] = s_block;
261	    }
262	}

264	// Phase B — owner-computes deterministic sum of all CTA slots, then the canonical
265	// d update. Runs AFTER the caller's grid barrier. Every CTA writes the same d
266	// (redundant but race-free); the apply reads ws.prodigy_d via st.d_factor.
267	__device__ inline void prodigy_precompute_reduce_phaseB(
268	        const PersistentContext& ctx, float d_prev, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
269	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
270	        // Fixed-order sums (ascending CTA index) — deterministic fp32.
271	        float r_sum = 0.0f, s_sum = 0.0f;
272	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) {
273	            r_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[c];
274	            s_sum += ws.prodigy_partials[ctx.n_ctas + c];
275	        }
276	        // Canonical d update (prodigy.h:56-65): d = max(d_prev, r/|s|).
277	        ws.prodigy_d[0] = algo::prodigy_update_d(d_prev, r_sum, s_sum);
278	    }
279	}

282	// (3b) STAGED — MUON: momentum update + Newton-Schulz orthogonalization.
283	//
284	// Shape: per-MATRIX, GRID-COOPERATIVE. A matmul is cross-element (X Xᵀ couples
285	// every row), and a realistic 2D weight does not fit one CTA's SMEM — so muon's
286	// precompute CANNOT follow the one-CTA-per-tensor element-wise model. All CTAs
287	// cooperate on ONE matrix at a time, with a grid barrier between each matmul and
288	// between NS iterations; the caller loops matrices.
289	//
290	// Semantic source — bindings.cpp::muon_fused_step (bindings.cpp:930-1014):
291	//   buf = momentum*buf + grad                    (bindings.cpp:948)
292	//   inv_norm = 1/(‖buf‖_F + 1e-7)                (bindings.cpp:962-963)
293	//   X = buf*inv_norm                             (bindings.cpp:964)
294	//   repeat ns_steps (default 5):                 (bindings.cpp:991-1007)
295	//       A   = X Xᵀ                               (bindings.cpp:992, torch::mm)
296	//       AX  = A X                                 (bindings.cpp:993)
297	//       AAX = A AX                                (bindings.cpp:994)
298	//       Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX  (a,b,c = 3.4445,-4.7750,2.0315; :938-940)
299	//   orth = final Y
300	//   scale = 0.2*sqrt(max(rows,cols)); neg_lr_scale=-lr*scale; decay=1-lr*wd
301	//                                                (bindings.cpp:980-983)
302	// Per-element bodies are CALLED from muon.h: muon_momentum_normalize_step
303	// (muon.h:33-46), muon_ns_combine_step (muon.h:49-60). The MATMULS are NEW
304	// device code: the live path delegates X Xᵀ etc. to torch::mm/cuBLAS
305	// (bindings.cpp:992-994), NOT a per-element canonical fn — so a tiled owner-
306	// computes matmul is legitimate and is cited to that mm sequence. The drift
307	// guard requires only that the ELEMENTWISE pieces call muon.h, which they do.
308	//
309	// DETERMINISM: the matmul is an owner-computes inner product per output element
310	// (one thread sums the k-dimension in ascending order — fixed fp32 order, no
311	// atomic). ‖buf‖_F² uses per-CTA slot publish → barrier → owner_sum (same as
312	// prodigy). 1D params are NOT handled here (they take the AdamW tail upstream,
313	// muon.h:75-76 / bindings.cpp:970-977).
314	//
315	// STAGE STRUCTURE (caller drives every grid barrier — one matrix per call):
316	//   muon_momentum_norm_phaseA → [barrier] → muon_norm_reduce_phaseB (writes
317	//     inv_norm) → [barrier] → muon_scale_X (X = buf*inv_norm)
318	//   then ns_steps × { muon_matmul A=XXᵀ → [barrier] → muon_matmul AX=A·X →
319	//     [barrier] → muon_matmul AAX=A·AX → [barrier] → muon_ns_combine_phase
320	//     (orth = a·X + b·AX + c·AAX) → [barrier] → swap(X, orth) }
321	//   The caller then binds st.orth=<final NS buffer>, st.neg_lr_scale,
322	//   st.decay_factor and runs apply_optimizer<Muon> (muon.h:63-73). The exact
323	//   barrier/swap sequence + stride args are in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md §3.
324	// ============================================================================
325	
326	static constexpr float kMuonNS_A = 3.4445f;   // bindings.cpp:938
327	static constexpr float kMuonNS_B = -4.7750f;  // bindings.cpp:939
328	static constexpr float kMuonNS_C = 2.0315f;   // bindings.cpp:940
329	static constexpr float kMuonNormEps = 1e-7f;  // bindings.cpp:962
330	
331	// momentum update Phase A: buf = momentum*buf + grad, accumulate ‖buf‖_F²
332	// partial per CTA. (We compute the norm from buf here, then scale X after the
333	// reduction — equivalent to bindings.cpp:948,962-964; we cannot scale X yet
334	// because inv_norm needs the full-matrix norm.) All CTAs cooperate over the
335	// flat [rows*cols] matrix via a grid-stride loop.
336	__device__ inline void muon_momentum_norm_phaseA(
337	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
338	        int64_t numel, float momentum,
339	        PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
340	    float nrm2 = 0.0f;
341	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
342	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
343	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
344	        // buf = momentum*buf + grad (plain SGD-momentum, muon.h:43-44 body).
345	        const float b = momentum * ws.muon_buf[i] + grad[i];
346	        ws.muon_buf[i] = b;
347	        nrm2 += b * b;
348	    }
349	    float blk = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(nrm2);
350	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) ws.muon_nrm_partials[blockIdx.x] = blk;
351	}
352	
353	// momentum norm Phase B (after grid barrier): owner-sum the per-CTA ‖buf‖_F²
354	// slots in fixed order, write inv_norm = 1/(sqrt(Σ) + 1e-7) (bindings.cpp:962-
355	// 963). The X = buf*inv_norm assignment is split off into muon_scale_X (below):
356	// the canonical muon_momentum_normalize_step (muon.h:33-46) does buf-update AND
357	// X-scale in one shot, but we need the FULL-MATRIX norm before we can scale, so
358	// phaseA folded grad into buf (the muon.h:43 body) and this reduction yields
359	// inv_norm — the X=buf*inv_norm step (a single multiply, bindings.cpp:964, NOT
360	// orthogonalization math) then runs post-barrier so every CTA sees the published
361	// norm. The orthogonalization MATH (the NS combine) stays on the canonical fn.
362	__device__ inline void muon_norm_reduce_phaseB(
363	        const PersistentContext& ctx, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
364	    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
365	        float s = 0.0f;
366	        for (unsigned c = 0; c < ctx.n_ctas; ++c) s += ws.muon_nrm_partials[c];
367	        ws.muon_inv_norm[0] = 1.0f / (sqrtf(s) + kMuonNormEps);
368	    }
369	}
370	
371	// X = buf * inv_norm (bindings.cpp:964). Single multiply (not optimizer math);
372	// runs after the barrier that publishes inv_norm. All CTAs grid-stride the flat
373	// matrix.
374	__device__ inline void muon_scale_X(int64_t numel, PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
375	    const float inv_norm = ws.muon_inv_norm[0];
376	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
377	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
378	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
379	        ws.muon_X[i] = ws.muon_buf[i] * inv_norm;
380	    }
381	}
382	
383	// Owner-computes tiled matmul C[m,n] = sum_k A[m,k] * B[k,n], grid-cooperative
384	// over the OUTPUT elements (one thread owns one output and sums the contraction
385	// in ASCENDING k — deterministic fp32, no atomic). `bT` selects B vs Bᵀ so we
386	// can express X Xᵀ (A=X[r,c], B=X[r,c] with bT → contract over c giving [r,r])
387	// and A X (contract over r) with one helper. Row-major [rows*cols] layout
388	// matching the flat workspace buffers.
389	//   - For A = X Xᵀ:  out[r1,r2] = Σ_c X[r1,c] X[r2,c]   (M=rows,N=rows,K=cols)
390	//   - For AX = A X:   out[r,c]   = Σ_j A[r,j] X[j,c]     (M=rows,N=cols,K=rows)
391	__device__ inline void muon_matmul(
392	        const float* __restrict__ A, const float* __restrict__ B,
393	        float* __restrict__ C, int M, int N, int K,
394	        int A_rowstride, int B_rowstride,
395	        bool b_transposed) {
396	    const int64_t total = (int64_t)M * N;
397	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
398	    for (int64_t idx = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
399	         idx < total; idx += gstride) {
400	        const int row = (int)(idx / N);
401	        const int col = (int)(idx % N);
402	        float acc = 0.0f;
403	        const float* arow = A + (int64_t)row * A_rowstride;
404	        if (b_transposed) {
405	            // B[col, k] (row `col` of B, length K). Used for X Xᵀ.
406	            const float* brow = B + (int64_t)col * B_rowstride;
407	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * brow[k];
408	        } else {
409	            // B[k, col]. Used for A X.
410	            for (int k = 0; k < K; ++k) acc += arow[k] * B[(int64_t)k * B_rowstride + col];
411	        }
412	        C[idx] = acc;
413	    }
414	}

416	// One Newton-Schulz iteration body's polynomial combine over the flat matrix:
417	// X_next = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX (muon.h:49-60, called per element). The matmuls
418	// A/AX/AAX must already be computed (by muon_matmul, with caller barriers
419	// between them). Writes into ws.muon_X in place is unsafe (combine reads X), so
420	// we combine into ws.muon_orth then the caller swaps orth↔X for the next iter,
421	// or — on the LAST iter — leaves the result in ws.muon_orth as the final
422	// orthogonalized direction.
423	__device__ inline void muon_ns_combine_phase(int64_t numel,
424	                                             PrecomputeWorkspace ws) {
425	    const int64_t gstride = (int64_t)blockDim.x * gridDim.x;
426	    for (int64_t i = (int64_t)blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
427	         i < numel; i += gstride) {
428	        // Canonical combine body (muon.h:49-60): Y = a*X + b*AX + c*AAX.
429	        algo::muon_ns_combine_step(ws.muon_orth, ws.muon_X, ws.muon_AX,
430	                                   ws.muon_AAX, kMuonNS_A, kMuonNS_B, kMuonNS_C,
431	                                   i);
432	    }
433	}

436	// (3c) STAGED — SUPERGROK11: meta-MLP mu (per element) + per-TENSOR cosine gate.
437	//
438	// Semantic source — supergrok11_fused_step (bindings.cpp:1339-1418) +
439	// sg11_mu_metanet_kernel (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:112-134) +
440	// compute_cosine_gate_fused (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:275-286).
441	//
442	// The live path does (bindings.cpp:1407-1416):
443	//   1. mu = rescale * phi(grad, sharpness)  with smart_grad = grad + 0*mu = grad
444	//      (mu_metanet called with alpha=0, so smart_grad == grad — the gate's first
445	//      argument IS grad).                          (bindings.cpp:1407-1409)
446	//   2. gate = clamp(cosine(grad, mu), 0, 1)        (bindings.cpp:1411 →
447	//      compute_cosine_gate_fused, supergrok11_sm90.cuh:275-286).
448	//   3. apply: g_eff = grad + lamb_eff*mu, Adam tail (lamb_eff = ramp*lamb*(1-
449	//      gate)*alpha). The fused TAIL apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11> (opt_components
450	//      .cuh:235-239 → sg11_sweep_b_step, supergrok11.h:79-111) reproduces the
451	//      SAME shape: smart_grad = g + (1-gate)*alpha*mu.
452	//
453	// Shape — PER-TENSOR, SINGLE-PHASE (NO grid barrier). The live per-op path
454	// (bindings.cpp:1407-1416) loops per parameter doing metanet→gate→adam, each
455	// tensor SELF-CONTAINED: gate(T) and apply(T) depend ONLY on mu(T), never on any
456	// other tensor's mu. So mu/gate/apply for one tensor fuse into ONE body that the
457	// SAME CTA owns end-to-end inside ONE task-queue drain — exactly the codegen's
458	// fused_optimizer_stage shape (fused_megakernel.cuh:101-142):
459	//   per claimed tensor T: { write mu(T)→global ; __syncthreads ; gate(T) via a
460	//   block tree (reads the mu it just wrote) ; apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11>(T) }.
461	// CRITICAL — this is NOT a full-queue mu pre-pass + a separate apply drain. That
462	// (rejected) shape would (a) need a grid barrier for cross-CTA mu visibility AND
463	// (b) SILENTLY NO-OP: the mu pre-pass drains the queue to n_tasks, so the apply
464	// drain's next_block() returns t>=n_tasks immediately and never applies (unless a
465	// sync_reset re-zeros the counter). The single-drain per-tensor form below has
466	// NO such hazard — one drain, no reset, no barrier, no race. (Prodigy DOES need a
467	// barrier because its d is a genuine cross-ALL-tensors reduction; SG11's gate is
468	// per-tensor — the cases are NOT analogous.)
469	//
470	//   mu(T)   — per ELEMENT: mu[idx] = rescale * sg11_phi_forward(grad[idx],
471	//             sharpness[idx], ...). Per-TENSOR weight set (W1,b1,W2,b2).
472	//   gate(T) — per TENSOR: cosine of (grad, mu) over THIS tensor, block tree
473	//             (block_reduce_sum_f32, primitives.cuh:125). NO cross-CTA, NO atomic.
474	//
475	// gate FORMULA — mirror the CODE, not the stale comment. compute_cosine_gate_
476	// fused (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:280-285) computes
477	//   num=Σ sg·mu; den_g=Σ sg·sg; den_m=Σ mu·mu;
478	//   gate = clamp(num / sqrt(den_g*den_m + 1e-12), 0, 1)
479	// with sg == grad here. It IGNORES gate_temp (the bindings.cpp:1276 comment
480	// claims a sigmoid(t·cos), but the function does a bare clamp — ref_sg11_step
481	// agrees: gate is the clamped cosine). We mirror the function.
482	//
483	// MODEL-COUPLED INPUT (flag loudly): `sharpness` is NOT optimizer state — it is
484	// (sam_grad − normal_grad)² from a SAM SECOND backward (sg11_sharpness_restore_
485	// kernel, supergrok11_sm90.cuh:236-248). It is a documented CONTRACT INPUT,
486	// exactly like looksam's sam_dir. CRUCIAL ABI GAP: FusedOptState (opt_components
487	// .cuh:84-113, which this header MUST NOT touch) has a `mu` field but NO
488	// `sharpness` field and NO phi-weight fields. So this stage takes sharpness +
489	// the phi weights as EXPLICIT pointers; the cell must supply a sharpness buffer
490	// the current ABI does not carry — see INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md.
491	// ============================================================================
492	
493	// Stage the per-tensor phi weights into SMEM ONCE per block (the codegen calls
494	// this before its per-tensor loop; same pattern as supergrok11_sm90.cuh:79-87).
495	// W1 is [H,2] row-major, b1/W2 are [H]. Caller provides the SMEM tiles.
496	template <int H>
497	__device__ __forceinline__ void sg_stage_phi_weights(
498	        const float* __restrict__ W1, const float* __restrict__ b1,
499	        const float* __restrict__ W2,
500	        float* sW1, float* sb1, float* sW2) {
501	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < H * 2; j += blockDim.x) sW1[j] = W1[j];
502	    for (int j = threadIdx.x; j < H;     j += blockDim.x) { sb1[j] = b1[j]; sW2[j] = W2[j]; }
503	    __syncthreads();
504	}
505	
506	// SG11 per-tensor body: write mu(T) to global, barrier, compute the per-tensor
507	// cosine gate(T) (reading the mu just written). Returns the clamped-cosine gate
508	// on EVERY thread (broadcast through the reduction smem) so the caller binds
509	// st.gate before apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11>. The phi weights are already in
510	// SMEM (sW1/sb1/sW2 from sg_stage_phi_weights). `off`/`n` is the tensor slice;
511	// the SAME CTA owns mu(T) and gate(T) — no cross-CTA dependency, no grid barrier.
512	template <int H>
513	__device__ inline float sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor(
514	        float* __restrict__ mu_blob,
515	        const float* __restrict__ grad,
516	        const float* __restrict__ sharpness,
517	        const float* sW1, const float* sb1, const float* sW2,
518	        float b2, float rescale,
519	        int64_t off, int n) {
520	    // mu(T): canonical meta-net forward (supergrok11.h:37-55) * rescale
521	    // (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:130), written to global mu_blob.
522	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
523	        const int64_t gi = off + i;
524	        const float g = grad[gi];
525	        const float s = sharpness[gi];
526	        const float phi = algo::sg11_phi_forward<H>(g, s, sW1, sb1, sW2, b2);
527	        mu_blob[gi] = rescale * phi;
528	    }
529	    // Barrier: every thread's mu writes for THIS tensor must be visible to the
530	    // gate reduction below (same block, so __syncthreads suffices — block-scope
531	    // visibility, no grid barrier).
532	    __syncthreads();
533	    // gate(T): clamped cosine of (grad, mu), block tree. sg == grad (alpha=0 path,
534	    // bindings.cpp:1408). gate_temp IGNORED (the function ignores it).
535	    float num = 0.0f, den_g = 0.0f, den_m = 0.0f;
536	    for (int i = threadIdx.x; i < n; i += blockDim.x) {
537	        const int64_t gi = off + i;
538	        const float sg = grad[gi];
539	        const float u  = mu_blob[gi];
540	        num   += sg * u;
541	        den_g += sg * sg;
542	        den_m += u  * u;
543	    }
544	    // Deterministic block reductions (fixed thread count). Three separate trees
545	    // (the live host fn does three independent .sum()s — same shape).
546	    num   = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(num);
547	    __syncthreads();
548	    den_g = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(den_g);
549	    __syncthreads();
550	    den_m = prim::block_reduce_sum_f32(den_m);
551	    // compute_cosine_gate_fused (supergrok11_sm90.cuh:283-285): denom =
552	    // sqrt(den_g*den_m + 1e-12); gate = (denom>0)? num/denom : 0; clamp[0,1].
553	    const float denom = sqrtf(den_g * den_m + 1e-12f);
554	    const float gate = (denom > 0.0f) ? (num / denom) : 0.0f;
555	    return fminf(fmaxf(gate, 0.0f), 1.0f);
556	}

561	// Semantic source — sg15_sweep_a_kernel (supergrok15_sm90.cuh:75-103) +

563	// sharpness) — IDENTICAL shape to SG11's mu sub-stage (the phi-net shares the
564	// SG11/SG15 form, supergrok15.h:34-52). The DIFFERENCE from SG11:
565	//   * gate is GLOBAL = sigmoid(training accuracy), set HOST-side and passed as a
566	//     scalar (supergrok15.h:85 gate_global; threaded via FusedScalars.gate,
567	//     opt_components.cuh:153). So there is NO gate REDUCTION stage for SG15.
568	//   * the per-coord alpha clip (sg15_alpha_per_coord, supergrok15.h:68-75) and
569	//     smart_grad = g + gate_global*a*mu happen INSIDE the apply tail
570	//     (apply_optimizer<SuperGrok15> → sg15_sweep_b_step, opt_components.cuh:240-
571	//     244). So the ONLY precompute SG15 needs is mu.
572	//   * sg15_sweep_a also accumulates a sharpness² partial (supergrok15_sm90.cuh
573	//     :99-102, sg15_sweep_a_step → supergrok15.h:56-65). That sum updates the
574	//     NEXT step's `sharpness` input host-side; it is NOT consumed by THIS step's
575	//     apply (the apply reads mu + the host gate). It is therefore part of the
576	//     model-coupled sharpness pipeline, NOT this step's optimizer precompute, and
577	//     is documented in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md rather than computed here.
578	//
579	// MODEL-COUPLED INPUT: same `sharpness` ABI gap as SG11 (FusedOptState has no
580	// sharpness field) — flagged in INTEGRATION-OPTSTAGES.md.
581	// ============================================================================
582	
583	// SG15 per-tensor body: write mu(T) to global. NO gate stage (the gate is the
